title: Find the City With the Smallest Number of Neighbors at a Threshold Distance
summary: Given n cities numbered from 0 to n-1, along with their bidirectional and weighted edges, find the city that has the smallest number of cities reachable within a given distance threshold.
statement: Given n cities numbered from 0 to n-1, along with their bidirectional and weighted edges, find the city that has the smallest number of cities reachable within a given distance threshold. If there are multiple cities with the same number of reachable cities, select the city with the highest number. The distance of a path between any two cities is the sum of the weights of the edges along that path.
constraints: Edges are undirected and weighted positively.
Minimize reachable other cities within threshold; ties choose greatest city index.
hints: All-pairs shortest paths make each reachability count explicit.
Initialize direct edges and zero diagonals, then run Floyd-Warshall.
Count other cities within threshold and minimize (count,-index).
Floyd-Warshall considers every possible intermediate city; -index implements the required greatest-index tie.
